2609.18385.title: Emotion Experience, Expression, and Perception: Emotion Analysis on Multimodal Social Media Posts
2609.18385.paper_summary: Emotions are an essential aspect of human communication, particularly on social media, where authors frequently combine text and images to convey their emotions. Yet prior work on emotion analysis of social media posts has overlooked two important aspects in regard to measuring how well readers can reconstruct the authors' intent: (1)~the image modality, with most work focusing solely on text, and (2)~the real-world events that trigger the expressed emotions, and their relationship to the post content. We therefore study the relation between (a) the author's experience of the event that caused them to write a social media post and (b) the content of the post, with a focus on readers' capability to reconstruct that emotion expression. To do that, we introduce the Multimodal Multi-Emotion-Model dataset Mult2EMo, created by collecting annotations from both authors and readers on the posts and their triggering events. We find that reconstruction is possible but challenging for both human readers and computational models. We show that understanding the triggering event is crucial for accurate reconstruction, and that reconstruction is particularly challenging when posts rely heavily on the image to express emotion.
2609.18385.paper_summary_zh: 情感是人類溝通中不可或缺的一個方面，特別是在社交媒體上，作者經常結合文本和圖像來傳達他們的情感。<lb/>然而，先前對社交媒體帖子情感分析的研究忽略了兩個重要方面，這些方面與衡量讀者能多好地重建作者的意圖有關： (1)~圖像模態，大多數研究僅專注於文本，和 (2)~觸發所表達情感的現實事件，以及它們與帖子內容的關係。<lb/>因此，我們研究 (a)~作者經歷的導致他們撰寫社交媒體帖子的事件和 (b)~帖子的內容之間的關係，重點放在讀者重建該情感表達的能力上。<lb/>為此，我們介紹了多模態多情感模型數據集 Mult2EMo，該數據集是通過收集作者和讀者對帖子及其觸發事件的註釋而創建的。<lb/>我們發現重建是可能的，但對於人類讀者和計算模型來說都具有挑戰性。<lb/>我們表明，理解觸發事件對於準確重建至關重要，並且當帖子在表達情感時過度依賴圖像時，重建特別具有挑戰性。
